name: DIASENSE
description: DIASENSE develops quantum diamond magnetic microscopes based on nitrogen-vacancy (NV) centers for contactless semiconductor chip failure analysis and defect detection. The Lyngby-based DTU spin-out joined the BioInnovation Institute (BII) Venture House 8 cohort and secured EUR 1.3M in follow-on BII funding in March 2026, bringing total funding to approximately EUR 1.8M. Its quantum diamond microscopy targets a chip-yield bottleneck where conventional methods cannot non-invasively map current flow inside packaged integrated circuits.
highlights: DTU spinout commercializing NV-center diamond microscopy for semiconductor metrology

news.title: DIASENSE new partner in Danish Quantum Community
news.excerpt: DIASENSE has joined Danish Quantum Community as a new partner. DIASENSE is a spin-out from The Technical University of Denmark founded in 2024 by Alexander Huck, Ulrik L. Andersen, Marvin Holten, and Christian Stig Dalsgaard Nielsen.

news.title: BII Backs Quantum Chip Diagnostic Startup Diasense With Additional €1.3 Million Investment
news.excerpt: Copenhagen's BioInnovation Institute provided Diasense with €1.3 million in follow-on financing, bringing its total investment in the quantum semiconductor diagnostics startup to €1.9 million.

news.title: Diasense Receives €1.3M ($1.5M USD) to Industrialize Quantum Diamond Microscopy
news.excerpt: Diasense, a Copenhagen-based quantum startup, has secured €1.3 million in follow-on funding from the BioInnovation Institute (BII) as part of the Venture House 8 cohort, bringing the company's total support from BII to €1.8 million.

news.title: Danish-Dutch quantum diamond microscope targets chip yield bottlenecks
news.excerpt: A Danish-Dutch consortium has secured about 5.7 million euros to develop a quantum-based failure analysis tool for the semiconductor industry. Led by Diasense, the NG-QDMM project includes 3.9 million euros from the Innovation Fund Denmark.
